subject.title: Codex-OAuth models fail over incorrectly — sibling model with healthy per-model quota still drops to non-codex fallback

question: For the remaining Codex OAuth sibling-model failover gap, should OpenClaw keep Codex OAuth models on the app-server and investigate the upstream websocket/rate-limit behavior, or make the direct OpenClaw Responses runtime a supported Codex path by adding Harmony tool-call parsing?
rationale: Both paths can plausibly address the remaining issue, but they change runtime ownership, tool-call parsing, and fallback behavior; source inspection and the open bookkeeping PR are not enough for automation to choose.

options.title: App-server first
options.body: Finish the model-scoped auth-profile fix, keep app-server as the default Codex runtime, and require live proof before changing direct-runtime routing.

options.title: Support direct Codex runtime
options.body: Sponsor a direct-runtime Harmony adapter and prove real Codex OAuth tool calls before allowing direct fallback for Codex models.

options.title: Wait for stronger live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open for additional quota-state logs or maintainer-run live proof before choosing either runtime path.

recommendation.title: App-server first
recommendation.body: Finish the model-scoped auth-profile fix, keep app-server as the default Codex runtime, and require live proof before changing direct-runtime routing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the most recent overlapping Codex app-server, OpenAI provider identity, and direct runtime history among the inspected paths.
